Strict coherent art direction matching the beige ink tavern reference and the inn image already shown: traditional hand-drawn BLACK pen contours, fine crosshatching and sparse stippling on warm light BEIGE/CREAM paper. Only black and beige tones; no other colors, no digital painting, photorealism or 3D. Medieval fantasy human-scale architecture, practical lived-in materials, clear believable perspective. Eye-level dialogue camera unless specified. Full bleed, no border or blank margin. No text, lettering, numbers, logos, UI, characters, faces, human silhouettes, animals, or creatures. Keep open staging at left and right foreground for separately overlaid character portraits; reduce texture and contrast there. Essential architecture and props should be visible in upper/middle 70%. Bottom quarter is quiet continuous flooring/ground for a later dialogue overlay, never an actual drawn panel. No invented quest solutions, faction emblems, political symbols, magic, or narrative revelations. Scene: intimate night storytelling gazebo, low close seated listener viewpoint looking toward low covered wooden platform on a worn stone base. Plain wooden roof and posts visible upper part, lateral step access, empty storyteller's bench and small plain side stand suitable for flasks. Peripheral benches only at far edges suggest places for listeners without drawing people. Protected lanterns illuminate platform with beige/cream paper light, ink hatching for night shadows, center stays spacious for narrator portrait. Indeterminate soft dark foliage around setting, no identifiable skyline, city monuments, portal or connecting road. No narrator, children, protagonist, bottles in hands or public silhouettes. Same ink-beige drawing style, never saturated night blue. IMPORTANT PALETTE: even SKY, distant views and windows must be warm beige/cream paper, NEVER blue, cyan or cool gray. Night sky if any is warm black ink on beige. Fire and lamplight are cream paper, no orange.
